title: MetaphorVU: Towards Metaphorical Video Understanding
claim: Metaphorical videos appear across many real-world settings, and understanding them requires reasoning beyond surface recognition to deeper implicit meanings.
layout: 2 panels, left video sources and categories, right top-down reasoning levels
description: The figure has two panels. The left panel is a grey column. At the top is a grid of social-media logos (YouTube, Vimeo, Reddit, TikTok, Twitter, Bilibili, Facebook, Weibo). Below it are five video thumbnails with play buttons, labeled Society Criticism, Life Contemplation, Value Advocacy, Relationship Insight and Situation Portrayal. The right panel is a top-down flow. It starts with a film strip of cartoon frames showing tailcoat pigs at a banquet and cats under the table. Next is a grey box for Recognition, which lists objects, and Event Description, which gives three event sentences joined by arrows. An italic orange note, 'We focus on a deeper level', leads to an orange Metaphor Understanding box. That box chains Visual Elements, Underlying Concepts and Implicit Meanings with orange arrows. It ends with the reading that a ruling group plunders social wealth. Orange marks the deeper level. Grey marks the surface level.
caption: Metaphorical videos are prevalent across various real-world scenarios to convey many complex ideas, and metaphorical video understanding requires high-order cognitive capabilities.
abstract: Metaphorical videos are prevalent across various real-world scenarios to convey complex ideas, and understanding them typically requires high-order cognitive capabilities. The lack of systematic studies on metaphorical video understanding not only constrains the real-world applicability of MLLMs but also impedes the thorough assessment of their high-order cognitive capabilities. To bridge this gap, we propose MetaphorVU-Bench, the first systematic and comprehensive benchmark dedicated to metaphorical video understanding. Through experiments, we find current MLLMs struggle with accurate metaphorical video understanding, lagging far behind human level, primarily due to defective cross-domain mapping. Motivated by this finding, we construct a metaphor knowledge graph as mapping augmentation and propose MetaphorBoost, an inference-time enhancement framework achieving consistent performance improvement. Our benchmark, analysis, and method provide useful insights and a foundation for future research on advancing MLLMs.
